Summary: 1. **Primary Request and Intent:** The user (Jan De Dobbeleer, maintainer of oh-my-posh) asked, across several turns: a. **Initial (analysis):** Analyze ohmyposh.dev's design, benchmark against competitors like Starship and other modern CLI-tool sites, iterate on a more modern/streamlined UI, and rethink the navigation architecture so it's "as straightforward to navigate to where you want to go as possible." Explicitly wanted **multiple proposals** — some close to what exists, some more dramatic. b. **Renderer architecture (a conversation that evolved over 5 turns):** Starting from "where does the studio logic come from to generate the themes?", the user progressively steered toward a specific architecture: - Move the imager to the web so `oh-my-posh-generate-image` could call an endpoint - Prefers a **render endpoint**, and asked TypeScript vs WASM - Proposed (and I confirmed as correct) writing a **new SVG writer as a sibling to the ANSI writer** rather than a separate imaging module that re-parses ANSI - Concluded **no JSON encoder is needed** — the Function returns SVG directly from config + pinned data - Wanted the SVG logic kept out of shipped artifacts **unless the diff removes more lines than it adds** (measured: it does, ≈ −1,500 lines, so no build tag) c. **Design direction chosen:** "I actually prefer the visual appearance of **direction A**. It's a lot cleaner, together with the **segment catalog** and the **studio direction** of B." d. **Execution instructions (verbatim):** *"start with the phase 0 website fixes, build a good plan, review the plan with Fable, and do the execution with Sonnet 5 in parallel where you can."* e. **Then:** *"go ahead with phase 1"* 2. **Key Technical Concepts:** - Docusaurus 3.10.2 (ESM config), Infima CSS framework, Algolia DocSearch, Azure Static Web Apps - Docusaurus specifics: `slug: /`, `unlisted: true`, `generated-index` category links, `link: {type: 'doc'}`, `_`-prefixed partials, `onBrokenLinks` / `onBrokenAnchors`, `@theme/Tabs`/`TabItem`/`CodeBlock`, CSS modules, `:global()` - Infima token system: `--ifm-color-primary-*` ramp, `--ifm-button-color`, `--ifm-font-color-base-inverse`, `--ifm-hero-background-color`, `--ifm-background-surface-color`, `--ifm-heading-line-height`, `--ifm-table-border-color` - WCAG contrast ratios; `resvg-wasm` for SVG→PNG - The `code-changes` skill workflow: Analyze → Plan → Delegate → Supervise → Verify → Deliver, with a stop gate after Analyze - Conventional commits 3. **Files and Code Sections:** **Analysis artifacts (scratchpad, not in repo):** - `C:\Users\jande\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--oh-my-posh\bf77db8f-a917-4fc4-be70-ca1927a57d56\scratchpad\omp-website-redesign.html` — the published proposal artifact - `...\scratchpad\phase0-plan.md` — Phase 0 plan (revised after Fable review) - `...\scratchpad\phase1-plan.md` — Phase 1 plan (revised after Fable review) **Published artifact:** `https://claude.ai/code/artifact/7e76d82e-c9b9-4c14-888b-d0e1f540d320` (favicon 🖥️) **Phase 0 — committed as `95ddb6ed`, `47c3efb0`, `81ecfd88`:** - `website/sidebars.js` — full rewrite. New top-level order: Overview (`index`) → Getting started → Configuration → Segments → Themes → Guides → faq → migrating → Contributing. Emoji removed from all labels. `Advanced` category (single child) folded into `Guides`. CLI order fixed `umbraco, unity, uno`. `generated-index` links with slugs `/getting-started`, `/installation`, `/themes-guide`, `/guides`, `/contributing`. - `website/docs/index.mdx` — **new**, the docs hub, `slug: /`, `id: index`, routing-only, under 40 lines - `website/docs/segments/overview.mdx` — **new**, `id: overview`, 117 segment links across 8 groups (cli, cloud, health, languages, music, scm, system, web) - `website/docs/configuration/introduction.mdx` — dropped `slug: /`, de-emojified `sidebar_label` - 13 docs de-emojified in `sidebar_label` frontmatter only - `website/docs/installation/next.md` → `_next.md`, `homebrew.md` → `_homebrew.md` (git-renamed), 3 importers updated (`windows.mdx`, `linux.mdx`, `macos.mdx`) - `website/static/llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `static/skills/ohmyposh/configuration.md` — dead `/docs/configuration/overview` links fixed - `website/src/css/custom.css` — removed `a.getStarted_Sjon`, `.themedImage_ToTc` pair, the whole `/* Dev settings */` block, `a.getStarted_src-pages-styles-module`, `.header-affiliate-link` rules. Added `--ifm-heading-font-weight: 600; --ifm-heading-line-height: 1.2;` and `h1,h2,h3{letter-spacing:-0.02em}`, `h1,h2{text-wrap:balance}` - `website/docusaurus.config.js` — navbar left = Docs / Segments (`docs/segments/overview`) / Themes (`docs/themes`) / Blog; Sponsor and Swag removed from navbar; `announcementBar` object deleted entirely; `og:image:width`/`og:image:height` removed from `metadata`; footer restructured — `Links` = Docusaurus + Privacy, new `Support` group = GitHub Sponsors + Product spotlight + **Swag** (added by me resolving a spec contradiction), `Sponsors` renamed `Our sponsors` - `website/static/skill.md`, `static/skills/ohmyposh/SKILL.md`, `static/llms.txt`, `static/llms-full.txt` — segment count phrasing corrected to "and more — 117 segments in all" **Read-only reference (Go side, for later phases):** - `src/cli/image/` — 1,877 lines total (`image.go` 920, `config.go` 98, `fonts.go` 95, tests 764). `image.go:236-246` downloads Hack.zip from GitHub at runtime; `image.go:462` uses one `spaceAdvance` constant (character grid); `image.go:498` has a "additional width for Nerd Font glyphs" fudge - `src/terminal/writer.go` — 1243+ lines, package-level globals (`builder`, `length`, `cellIndex`, `foregroundColor`, `currentColor`, `bgGradientCells`), no `Writer` interface - `src/cli/data.go` — `applyDataFile(flags, changed)` sets `flags.SegmentData`/`flags.EnvData`, making the engine hermetic - `src/segments/http.go:27` — `url := h.options.String(URL, "")` — arbitrary URL from config - `website/export_themes.mjs` — shells out to `oh-my-posh config export image --config X --output Y --background-color Z --data segment_data.json` - `website/static/codepoints.csv` — 1,939 Nerd Font glyph mappings, consumed by `src/config/migrate_glyphs.go` - `.github/workflows/docs.yml:40` — runs `npm run themes` (CI only) **Memory:** - `C:\Users\jande\.claude\projects\D--oh-my-posh\memory\website-redesign-direction.md` — created, records Direction A + catalog + studio, and the SVG-encoder architecture - `MEMORY.md` — one pointer line appended 4. **Errors and fixes:** - **Wrong claim that `auth.mdx` should be added to the sidebar.** The first IA agent reported it as an "orphaned doc". I read `Auth.js` and corrected myself: it renders OAuth tokens from the query string, so it is a callback landing page, not documentation. Fix: `unlisted: true`, deliberately kept out of the sidebar. - **Phase 0 plan told the implementer to *restore* the themedImage filters under a new class.** Fable proved this false: Docusaurus 3.10 `ThemedImage` delegates to `ThemedComponent` (emits `themedComponent` classes), so the selectors were already dead and the Store badge renders correctly unfiltered because `windows.mdx` already theme-swaps `msstore-dark.svg`/`msstore-light.svg`. Reapplying the invert would have rendered it dark-on-dark. Fix: plain deletion, no replacement, and the `windows.mdx` edit dropped from Task B (which also removed the only file overlap between tasks A and B). - **Emoji removal was undeliverable at the stated scope.** 14 docs carry emoji in `sidebar_label` frontmatter, not in `sidebars.js`. Would have shipped a half-emoji sidebar. Fix: added those 13 files (plus introduction) to Task A. - **Phantom "Personal" segment group** in the plan; the eighth group is Health. Fix: corrected, and told the implementer to derive groups from disk. - **Wrong rationale for `onBrokenLinks`.** I claimed `'ignore'` was why the `llms.txt` rot went unnoticed; `onBrokenLinks` never inspects `static/`. All 39 absolute `/docs/...` targets already resolved, so fallout was near-zero, not "real hits". Fix: corrected the rationale and the risk estimate. - **Missed `static/skills/ohmyposh/configuration.md:121`** (same dead link) and **missed the `next.md`/`homebrew.md` partials** building as sitemapped junk pages. Fix: both folded into Task A. - **Phase 1 plan said "scope white text to the primary button only."** Fable proved this fails WCAG: Infima's `--ifm-button-color` = `--ifm-font-color-base-inverse` = near-black `#1c1e21` in dark mode, precisely because dark primary `#5c9fee` is light. White on `#5c9fee` = 2.75:1, below even the 3:1 large-text bar; Infima's own value gives 6.1:1. Fix: delete `.getStarted` entirely and let Infima colour both buttons. - **Phase 1 plan claimed removing `hero--primary` un-darkens the hero.** False — Infima's base `.hero` paints `--ifm-hero-background-color` → `--ifm-background-surface-color` = `#242526` against page `#1b1b1d` in dark mode, and no task owned the fix. Fix: Task E drops the `hero` class outright; `hero__title`/`hero__subtitle` are font-size-only and stay. - **F2 spec self-contradiction:** said "Add Swag to the existing `Links` group" AND "After the change, `Links` holds only `Docusaurus` and `Privacy`." The Task F agent correctly stopped and reported rather than guessing, leaving `swag.ohmyposh.dev` unplaced. Fix: I placed Swag in the `Support` group (it's a revenue channel). - **F2 also risked duplicating "Product spotlight"** — spec said move Sponsor out of `Links` but never Product spotlight. Fix: spec amended to say move both. - **Verification greps were unscoped** and would hit `node_modules/infima` (which defines `.hero__title`). Fix: scoped to `src`, `docs`, `blog`, `docusaurus.config.js`. - **I incorrectly claimed the Victor Mono `/static/fonts/VictorMono.ttf` path was a live 404.** Webpack rewrites the `@font-face` url either way, so the font always loaded. Reported this correction to the user honestly; the fix is still right but cosmetic. - **Phase 0's own count fix introduced an off-by-semantics error:** "and 117 other segments" after listing four examples reads as 121. Fixed all four agent-facing files to "and more — 117 segments in all". Task E had reproduced the same construction in a feature card; corrected, plus a hyphen → em dash. - **Task G set `line-height: 1.2` on a bare `h1, h2, h3` element rule**, which would lose specificity fights with `.markdown h1`. I moved it to `--ifm-heading-line-height`. - **Correction to Fable's own reasoning (noted to the user):** Infima *does* define `--ifm-button-background-color: #0000` for `.button--outline`, so the bare outline button's border was not collapsing. Adding `button--primary` is still correct (accent border + hover) but the stated cause was wrong. The `color: #fff` diagnosis was correct — `.button--outline:not(.button--active):not(:hover){color:var(--ifm-font-color-base)}` is what it defeated. - **Build broken-anchor warning `/docs/themes#jandedobbeleer`** — investigated: `docs/themes.md` is 18 lines locally; the 124 theme sections are generated by `npm run themes`, which only runs in CI. It's a local-only artifact, so `onBrokenAnchors` deliberately stays at `'warn'`. - **Browser pane could not screenshot** ("the Browser pane is not displayed, so the page is not compositing frames"). Worked around by using `get_page_text`, `read_page`, and `javascript_tool` to extract computed styles and design tokens instead. Also hit a transient tab-identity bug where JS executed against a stale origin (ghostty instead of atuin) — abandoned that sampling since the research agent covered it. 5. **Problem Solving:** Established the core architectural insight for the renderer work: today's flow (`engine → terminal writer → ANSI → image.go re-parses ANSI → pixels`) discards information and then tries to recover it. The fix is to extract a **run stream** between resolver and encoder in `terminal/`, then SVG becomes one encoder among several. SVG is already structured output (`data-segment`/`data-block` attributes), so no JSON encoder is needed. Pinning the data file in the Function makes the SSRF guard fall out of the design. Measured the deletion at ≈ −1,500 lines and −3 dependencies, which settles the build-tag question (no tag needed). Established the font strategy matrix: local `--format svg` references the family by name; the gallery inlines SVG and uses a site-hosted subset woff2; shareable files embed a subset as data URI; GitHub READMEs need PNG because GitHub sanitizes SVG and strips `

Phase 1 shipped. Seven commits total across both phases, tree clean, build green.

```bash
git log --oneline -4
```

| | |
|---|---|
| `e67d23e9` | homepage rebuilt around the install command |
| `21e762cb` | Segments + Themes in primary nav, sponsor bar retired |
| `d3129676` | accent recalibrated, dark ramp added |
| `17615915` | segment count phrasing |

**Verified from build output, not agent claims:**
- `<header class="heroBanner_UJJx">` — both Infima `hero` classes gone
- Navbar: Docs · Segments · Themes · Blog, both new targets resolving; Sponsor and Swag absent
- All 11 footer URLs present exactly once, including Swag
- Three install commands byte-exact against the docs
- `og:image` retained, width/height gone
- No `#173448` or `#2c7ae0` anywhere in built CSS
- Cascade order correct — Infima light default @1849, ours @14512, dark ramp @53627
- No `.getStarted` rule survives; `hero.png` has explicit dimensions and its own module class

**Three things I got wrong that got caught:**
1. My Phase 1 spec contradicted itself on Swag — "add to Links" *and* "Links holds only Docusaurus and Privacy". Task F stopped and asked instead of guessing, which was the right call. Resolved by putting Swag in `Support`, since buying merch is a revenue channel, not a miscellaneous link.
2. Task E reproduced the "and 117 other segments" construction I'd just fixed elsewhere. Corrected — the card title carries the count, so the body says "and more".
3. Task G set heading `line-height` on a bare element selector, which loses to `.markdown h1`. Moved to the token.

**Follow-ups now queued but not done:**
- A real 1200×630 social card. The og:image is a 1100×44 prompt strip — the false dimensions are gone, but the card is still the wrong shape.
- `onBrokenAnchors` stays at `warn`. The single warning is local-only: `themes.md` is 18 lines in the repo and CI generates the 124 theme sections via `npm run themes`.

Next in the plan is Phase 2 — the golden-file harness over all 124 bundled themes, then extracting the run stream from `terminal/writer.go`. That one's a different animal: it touches the prompt hot path, so the gate is byte-identical ANSI plus a clean benchstat, and it should not be delegated the way these were.

Proposal B had some really great design for the segment catalog, and I really want that implemented first. There's the additional feedback that I have regarding the home page as well.

If you now look at the flow on a desktop, it doesn't really feel right because it has a large header-like prompt that knows where you are, and then a subtext. It goes from white to small, back to white again. It just overall feels like there's so much white space here that makes it rather difficult or not really that pleasing to read.

I don't know what we can do about it, maybe alignment or other things. Same as with the hero cards at the bottom initially, I think in design A it had a card design with rounded corners. That's all gone now, so there's a lot we can still do to improve and put a cherry on top.

Here is the original readout for the segments section from the design document we created:

The same language applied to the 117-segment catalog
Facets with live counts, a URL that encodes filter state, and a badge column carrying the metadata people actually search on: does it need auth, is it cached, does it need a Nerd Font. This is the Tauri plugin-grid pattern, which was the only real in-browser filter found in the whole cohort.

# Code Changes

The workflow for going from an issue, pull request, idea, or feature request to shipped code.
Follow the phases in order. Analysis always comes first; code comes last.

Each phase has a reference file with the full instructions. **Read the reference file when you
enter the phase** — not before, and never skip it because the phase "looks obvious".

## Roles

Assign work based on model capability. The coordinator is not the strongest model — it's the one
that stays resident, owns every phase by default, and knows when it's out of its depth.

| Role        | Capability tier                                               | Owns                                                                          |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Coordinator | Capable mid-tier, resident for the whole task                | Analysis, plan, delegation, supervision, verification, delivery — by default |
| Escalation  | Strongest reasoning model available; invoked only on trigger | The specific judgment call the coordinator flagged, then control returns     |
| Implementer | Same tier as coordinator, or smaller for trivial edits        | Executing one pinned, self-contained task                                    |

Concrete model names per vendor (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) and how to run the split in Claude
Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, or IDE agents: [references/model-tiers.md](references/model-tiers.md).

When the current agent already runs at implementer tier, there's no separate delegation step for
standard work: plan and execute directly, still following every phase. Escalate to the strongest
model only when a trigger fires — see [references/escalate.md](references/escalate.md) — never by
default and never for a routine judgment call the coordinator is equipped to make itself.

## The flow

1. **Analyze** ([references/analyze.md](references/analyze.md)) — root cause and scope,
   validated against the code, never against the report alone.
2. **Plan** ([references/plan.md](references/plan.md)) — pinned spec, task split, parallel vs
   sequential, workspace per task.
3. **Delegate** ([references/delegate.md](references/delegate.md)) — match each task to the
   right executor, coordinator-tier by default.
4. **Supervise** ([references/supervise.md](references/supervise.md)) — monitor, unblock, and
   critically review implementer output.
5. **Verify** ([references/verify.md](references/verify.md)) — quality gates plus functional
   proof, never delegated downward.
6. **Deliver** ([references/deliver.md](references/deliver.md)) — conventional commits and an
   outcome-first report.

Analyze, Supervise, and Verify each carry an escalation checkpoint — see
[references/escalate.md](references/escalate.md) — for handing one specific judgment call to the
strongest available model without giving up ownership of the phase.

**Stop gate:** Phase 1 ends with reporting the analysis and proposed approach to the user and
waiting for a go. Skip the gate only when the user already gave the go in the request itself
("do it", "fix it and commit", "implement with Sonnet").

## Special cases

These entry points replace or extend Phase 1; the rest of the flow applies unchanged.

- Pull request review comments →
  [references/pr-review-comments.md](references/pr-review-comments.md)
- Issue triage → [references/issue-triage.md](references/issue-triage.md)


ARGUMENTS: Implement Proposal B segment catalog (faceted, live counts, URL filter state, badge column) + homepage flow/rhythm fixes and card design for feature cards

4	No code gets written or edited during this phase.
5

7	
8	- Issues and PRs: `gh issue view <n> --comments` / `gh pr view <n> --comments`, plus linked

10	- Ideas and verbal requests: restate the goal and constraints in your own words. If the request

18	fact and gives Phase 5 its verification case for free. When reproduction is impossible (platform,

22

Repo: D:\oh-my-posh (oh-my-posh, Go + Docusaurus website).

I need to build a faceted, filterable segment catalog page on the website. Facets planned: category, "needs auth", "is cached", "needs a Nerd Font". I need to know what metadata already exists and where the source of truth is.

Investigate and report precisely (file:line):

1. `website/docs/segments/**/*.mdx` — what frontmatter fields do these files carry today? Show the exact frontmatter of 4-5 representative files across different groups (e.g. scm/git, web/http, languages/golang, health/withings, cli/npm). Is it uniform? content.text: ## Analysis ### Homepage — found the cause Direction A's hero was **left-aligned, gap `1.1rem`**, install box a single bordered unit, prompt on a dark rounded card, features as bordered cards: ```css .mock-a .m-hero { padding: 2.5rem 0 2.75rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1.1rem; } .mock-a .card { border: 1px solid var(--a-rule); border-radius: 9px; padding: 0.95rem 1rem; } .mock-a .termcard { background: var(--a-deep); border-radius: 9px; } ``` Phase 1 shipped `text-align: center`, `align-items: center`, `gap: 2rem`, no card, bare `` ([styles.module.css:8-76](website/src/pages/styles.module.css:8)). Centering deletes the shared left edge that held the stack together; doubling the gap turns five elements into five islands. That is the "white, small, white" bounce — nothing anchors the eye. Infima note: `col--4` carries padding gutters, so a border on `.feature` itself makes cards touch. Cards need an inner `div`. ### Segment catalog — three of the four proposed facets are not real I checked each against source rather than trusting the design doc: | Facet | Verdict | Evidence | |---|---|---| | Cacheable | **dead** — 117/117 | `Cache *Cache` is on the generic struct, [segment.go:44](src/config/segment.go:44). Doc's "61" was mockup filler | | Async | **dead** | top-level config flag, not per-segment | | Needs Nerd Font | **dead, wrong tier** | 0/117 segment docs and 2/110 Go segment files contain a PUA codepoint. Icons come from the *theme*. Belongs on the themes gallery | | Needs auth | **real, ~8** | `APIKey`/`AccessToken`/`RefreshToken` reads: brewfather, copilot, lastfm, nightscout, owm, strava, todoist, withings. True OAuth is 3 | | Group | **real, 8** | derivable from directory | Replacements that are true and actually discriminating: **group**, **needs a token or account**, **hits the network every prompt**, **platform-limited** (`winget`, `winreg` gate on GOOS). Free-text search stays the highest-value control regardless. ### Data source — better than expected `## What` is uniform across all 117 docs and its first paragraph is a usable one-liner. Title and path come from frontmatter and directory. So cards generate at build time — no 117-entry hand-authored file, only the two small curated flag lists, which a test can pin against the Go source. ### Out of scope Themes gallery, per-segment live previews (needs the Phase 2 renderer), FAQ split.

questions.question: Where should the catalog live? `docs/segments/overview` is currently the sidebar category link (sidebars.js:63) and llms.txt points at it.

options.label: Standalone /segments (Recommended)
options.description: New src/pages/segments.js — full width, no docs sidebar competing with the facet rail. Navbar retargets to /segments. docs/segments/overview stays as the plain grouped link list for the sidebar and LLM consumers, with a link across. Costs one redundant-looking index.

options.label: Inside docs/segments/overview
options.description: Catalog replaces the bullet list as an imported React component. One index, keeps the URL, sidebar and Algolia unchanged. But the docs left sidebar sits next to the facet rail — two rails, card grid squeezed to roughly 60% width.

options.label: Standalone, and delete the docs index
options.description: Cleanest single source of truth. Requires rewiring the sidebar category to a generated-index and fixing the llms.txt and skill.md links that Phase 0 just repaired.

questions.question: Card descriptions get generated from each doc's `## What` first paragraph. Those contain reference-style links like `[Git][git]` and inline code.

options.label: Strip markup, use as-is (Recommended)

The mockup's "61" was filler. - **Async** — not a segment property. - **Needs Nerd Font** — not a segment property at all. Belongs on the themes gallery. Shipping it here would be a lie on 117 cards. Dropping these is deliberate and is the main deviation from the approved design. A facet that matches everything is not a filter; it is decoration that costs a click to discover. ### The credential tiers (curated, 11 entries) | Tier | Label | Segments | | --- | --- | --- | | `oauth` | Sign in via ohmyposh.dev | strava, withings | | `cli` | Run `oh-my-posh auth` | copilot, ytm | | `apikey` | API key in your config | lastfm, owm, todoist, brewfather | | `url` | Token inside the URL you supply | nightscout, wakatime, http | Authoritative for `cli`: `src/cli/auth.go:23-26` (`ValidArgs: copilot, ytmda`). Authoritative for `oauth`: `src/segments/strava.go:17`, `src/segments/withings.go:79` embed `http.OAuthRequest`. The other two tiers are doc-derived and hand-curated. --- ## Workstream 1 — the catalog ### Placement (decided) Standalone `/segments` page. Full width, no docs sidebar competing with the facet rail. `docs/segments/overview.mdx` keeps its grouped link list — it is the sidebar category target (`sidebars.js:63-68`) and `llms.txt` points at it — and gains a link across to `/segments`. ### Data contract — PINNED Both Task A and Task B build against this exact shape. Neither may change it. ```js // window[...].globalData['oh-my-posh-segments'].default { segments: [ { id: 'golang', // doc filename without extension; the URL slug type: 'go', // the string you put in your config `type` field name: 'Golang', // frontmatter `title` group: 'languages', // directory name groupLabel: 'Languages', // display label href: '/docs/segments/languages/golang', description: 'Display the currently active Golang version.', auth: null, // or 'oauth' | 'cli' | 'apikey' | 'url' }, // ... 117 entries, sorted by name within group ], groups: [ { id: 'cli', label: 'CLI', count: 39 }, // ... 8 entries, sorted by count descending ], authTiers: [ { id: 'oauth', label: 'Sign in via ohmyposh.dev', count: 2 }, { id: 'cli', label: 'Run oh-my-posh auth', count: 2 }, { id: 'apikey', label: 'API key in your config', count: 4 }, { id: 'url', label: 'Token in your URL', count: 3 }, ], } ``` `group` values are the eight directory names: `cli`, `cloud`, `health`, `languages`, `music`, `scm`, `system`, `web`. `groupLabel` for `scm` is `Source control`; the rest are the capitalised directory name except `CLI`. ### Task A — build-time data plugin **Owns, and creates:** `website/plugins/segments/index.js`, `website/plugins/segments/data.js`. Touches nothing else. Does **not** edit `docusaurus.config.js` — the coordinator wires it up. CommonJS, matching `website/plugins/appinsights/index.js`. Shape: ```js module.exports = function (context, options) { return { name: 'oh-my-posh-segments', async loadContent() { /* read + validate, return the object above */ }, async contentLoaded({ content, actions }) { actions.setGlobalData(content); }, }; }; ``` `loadContent` steps: 1. Walk `/website/docs/segments/*/` for `*.mdx`, skipping `overview.mdx`. Derive `group` from the directory, `id` from the filename. 2. Parse frontmatter for `title`. Do not add a YAML dependency — the frontmatter is three flat `key: value` lines in all 117 files; a line scan between the two `---` fences is correct and has no failure mode here. If a file's frontmatter lacks `title`, throw. 3. Extract the description: the first non-empty paragraph after the `## What` heading, joined onto one line. Then normalise: - `[text][ref]` and `[text](url)` → `text` - `` `code` `` → `code` - collapse runs of whitespace - if it does not end in `.`, `!` or `?`, leave it alone (do not invent punctuation) If `## What` is missing or its first paragraph is empty, throw naming the file. 4. Read `/src/config/segment_types.go`. Parse the constant block (`^\t([A-Z0-9_]+)\s+SegmentType = "([a-z0-9_-]+)"$`) and the registry map body that starts at `var Segments = map[SegmentType]func() SegmentWriter{` (`^\t([A-Z0-9_]+):`). Resolve map keys to type strings. 5. **Assert, throwing a message that names the offenders:** - every registry key resolves to a declared constant - every registered type has a doc file, after applying `TYPE_TO_DOC_ID` and skipping `IGNORED_TYPES` - every doc file maps back to a registered type - every key in the override maps corresponds to a known doc id A build must fail loudly when a segment is added to Go and not documented, or vice versa. That guard is the reason this is a plugin and not a committed JSON file. 6. Attach `auth` from `AUTH_TIERS`, `description` overrides from `DESCRIPTION_OVERRIDES`. 7. Compute `groups` and `authTiers` counts from the assembled list, never hardcode them. `website/plugins/segments/data.js` holds the curated tables and nothing else: ```js const TYPE_TO_DOC_ID = { go: 'golang', copilot_cli: 'copilot-cli' }; const IGNORED_TYPES = new Set(['exit']); // legacy alias for `status` const AUTH_TIERS = { strava: 'oauth', withings: 'oauth', copilot: 'cli', ytm: 'cli', lastfm: 'apikey', owm: 'apikey', todoist: 'apikey', brewfather: 'apikey', nightscout: 'url', wakatime: 'url', http: 'url' }; const AUTH_TIER_LABELS = { oauth: 'Sign in via ohmyposh.dev', cli: 'Run oh-my-posh auth', apikey: 'API key in your config', url: 'Token in your URL' }; const GROUP_LABELS = { cli: 'CLI', cloud: 'Cloud', health: 'Health', languages: 'Languages', music: 'Music', scm: 'Source control', system: 'System', web: 'Web' }; const DESCRIPTION_OVERRIDES = {}; // filled by the coordinator after reviewing the extraction ``` Every one of `IGNORED_TYPES`, `TYPE_TO_DOC_ID` and the tier assignments carries a comment saying why. A reader six months out must not have to re-derive that `exit` is an alias. **Deliverable beyond the code:** write the 117 extracted descriptions, one per line as `id\tdescription`, to `C:\Users\jande\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--oh-my-posh\6c0a282a-886f-458d-a426-93d95104b4a6\scratchpad\extracted-descriptions.tsv`. The coordinator reviews that and authors the overrides. Do not write overrides yourself. ### Task B — catalog component and page **Owns, and creates:** `website/src/components/SegmentCatalog/index.js`, `website/src/components/SegmentCatalog/styles.module.css`, `website/src/pages/segments.js`. Touches nothing else. Build against the pinned contract above. Read it with: ```js import { usePluginData } from '@docusaurus/useGlobalData'; const { segments, groups, authTiers } = usePluginData('oh-my-posh-segments'); ``` Layout — mirrors the approved mockup, retoned onto Infima tokens so it is theme-aware (the mockup was drawn in Direction B's fixed dark palette; do not hardcode those colours): - Two-column grid, `13.5rem 1fr`, collapsing to one column under 700px where the facet rail becomes a top strip with a bottom border instead of a right border. - **Facet rail** — one `
` per facet group, legend styled as the mockup's `.lbl` (monospace, `0.62rem`, `letter-spacing: 0.15em`, uppercase, muted). Real `` elements, visually restyled — do not fake them with spans, the mockup did that only because it was static artwork. Each row shows its count right-aligned in monospace with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`. - **Counts are live**: each facet's count reflects what selecting it would yield given the *other* currently-active facets and the search term. A facet whose count is 0 stays visible but is disabled and dimmed — never removed, because a rail that reflows on every keystroke is unusable. - Within one facet group, checks are OR'd. Across groups, AND'd. - **Search** over `name`, `type`, `id` and `description`, case-insensitive, substring. **Do not bind ⌘K or Ctrl-K** — Algolia DocSearch already owns that chord sitewide. No global keyboard shortcut at all; a plain labelled input. - **Result grid** — `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(190px, 1fr))`, gap `0.7rem`. Each card is a `` to `href`, `border: 1px solid var(--ifm-color-emphasis-200)`, `border-radius: 8px`, `background: var(--ifm-background-surface-color)`, hover raises the border to the accent. Card contents, in order: the `type` string in monospace as the primary name; the description; a tag row. - **Tags**: the group label always; `needs auth` when `auth` is set, in the warning tone (`--ifm-color-warning-darkest` on light, lightest on dark) with `title` set to the tier label. Tags are ``, not links. - The `type` is the headline because it is the string a user types into their config. Where `type !== id`, that distinction is exactly the thing they need and cannot get from the sidebar today. Show `name` as secondary text on the card when it differs meaningfully. - A results count line above the grid: `117 segments` / `9 of 117 segments`. - An empty state when the filter matches nothing, with a button that clears all filters. **URL state:** ```js import { useHistory, useLocation } from '@docusaurus/router'; ``` - `?group=cli,cloud&auth=oauth&q=kube`. Omit any key that is empty. Never write `?` alone. - Read with `new URLSearchParams(useLocation().search)` — same idiom as `src/components/Auth.js:6`. - Write with `history.replace`, not `push`, so typing in the search box does not bury the back button under one entry per keystroke. - Initial state comes from the URL, so a shared link restores the view. - **SSR safety:** never touch `window` or `document` during render. On the server `useLocation().search` is `''`, which must render the full unfiltered list — that is also what makes the page indexable and what Algolia will crawl. No `BrowserOnly` wrapper; the whole page must server-render. `website/src/pages/segments.js` is a thin wrapper: `` containing a short header (`

Segments

` plus one sentence and a link to the configuration reference) and ``. Derive the count from the data; do not hardcode `117` in JSX. Match repo conventions: plain function declarations, `export default X;` at the bottom, `import React from 'react'`, CSS modules, `classnames` for conditional classes. ### Task D — the docs index **Owns:** `website/docs/segments/overview.mdx`. Touches nothing else. Keep the eight grouped lists exactly as they are — they are the sidebar's index and what `llms.txt` and the skill files point at. Change only the intro paragraph so it routes to the catalog first, in the house voice (plain, no marketing register, no exclamation): > A segment is a single piece of information in your prompt — the current path, a Git status, > a language version, a cloud context. See [Segment][segment] for how to configure one. > > To search and filter all 117 segments, use the [segment catalog](/segments). The full list > follows, grouped by category. Do not renumber, reorder or reword the lists themselves. ### Coordinator-owned `website/docusaurus.config.js` — add `'./plugins/segments'` to `plugins`, retarget the navbar `Segments` item from `docs/segments/overview` to `/segments`. Two edits, no delegation, so no task contends for this file. --- ## Workstream 2 — homepage rhythm ### Task C **Owns:** `website/src/pages/index.js`, `website/src/pages/styles.module.css`. Touches nothing else. The complaint is real and the cause is specific: Direction A's hero was **left-aligned with a `1.1rem` gap**. What shipped is centred with a `2rem` gap. Centring removes the shared left edge that gave the stack a spine; doubling the gap turns five elements into five islands with nothing to hold them. Reference, from the approved mockup: ```css .mock-a .m-hero { padding: 2.5rem 0 2.75rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1.1rem; } .mock-a .card { border: 1px solid var(--a-rule); border-radius: 9px; padding: 0.95rem 1rem; } .mock-a .termcard { background: var(--a-deep); border-radius: 9px; margin-top: 0.5rem; } ``` Changes: 1. **Left-align the hero.** Drop `text-align: center` from `.heroBanner`; set `align-items: flex-start` on `.heroBanner :global(.container)`; drop the centring from `.installNote`; `.buttons` gets `justify-content: flex-start`. Under 700px it stays left-aligned — do not re-centre on mobile, the spine matters more on a narrow column. 2. **Tighten the rhythm.** Container `gap: 1.1rem`. Then give the install box a little more air above it than the title/subtitle pair gets, via a `margin-top` on `.installBox` of about `0.9rem` — the point is that title+subtitle read as one unit and the install cluster as another, rather than five evenly spaced strangers. 3. **Cap the measure.** `.subtitle` `max-width: 52ch` (currently `640px`). The `h1` gets `max-width: 20ch` so it breaks into two lines and forms a block rather than one long rule of text. 4. **The prompt gets a card.** Wrap the `` in a `div` with a dark background (`#10243c`, Direction A's `--a-deep`), `border-radius: 9px`, and padding. Keep the `img` element's `width`/`height`/`alt` attributes exactly as they are — they were verified in Phase 1 and prevent layout shift. 5. **Feature cards come back.** Infima's `col--4` carries horizontal padding as its gutter, so a border on `.feature` itself makes the cards touch edge to edge. Put an inner `
` inside each column and border that: `border: 1px solid var(--ifm-color-emphasis-200)`, `border-radius: 9px`, `padding: 1.15rem 1.25rem`, `background: var(--ifm-background-surface-color)`, and `height: 100%` so the three cards align at the bottom regardless of copy length. 6. **Break up the whitespace.** Give `.features` a `border-top: 1px solid var(--ifm-color-emphasis-200)` and honest vertical padding (about `3rem 0`), and drop the stray `display: flex; align-items: center` it carries today — it is a block section, and the flex there does nothing but make the rule harder to reason about. 7. Leave the copy alone. Titles, install commands, feature text, shell list: unchanged. Do not touch `website/src/css/custom.css`. The accent ramp landed in Phase 1 and is correct. --- ## Verification (coordinator, not delegated) 1. `npm run build` clean. `onBrokenLinks` is `'throw'`, so `/segments` must resolve; the only tolerated warning is the known local-only `/docs/themes#jandedobbeleer` anchor, which CI generates via `npm run themes`. 2. Grep the built HTML for `/segments` — assert all 117 cards server-render with no filters, which is both the SEO and the Algolia requirement. 3. Assert the built page contains `>go<` and `>copilot_cli<` — proof the card headline is the config type and not the doc id. 4. Break the guard on purpose: temporarily add a bogus `SegmentType` to the Go registry and confirm the build fails naming it. Revert. 5. Load `/segments?group=cloud&q=azure` in the browser pane and confirm the checkboxes and the search box come back checked and filled. 6. Confirm no `⌘K` / `Ctrl+K` handler was added — Algolia owns that chord. 7. Homepage: confirm the hero container computes `align-items: flex-start` and the feature cards report a non-zero `border-width`. 8. Confirm `--ifm-color-primary` and the Phase 1 dark ramp are untouched in the built CSS. ## Out of scope Themes gallery, per-segment live previews (needs the Phase 2 renderer), the FAQ split, `themes/schema.json` as a data source, and any Go change.

Four agents running. Where things stand:

**Review caught six defects worth having.** The two that would have shipped broken:

1. **My Nerd Font scan was wrong.** I searched for literal PUA characters; this repo writes glyphs as `\uXXXX` escapes. Real count is 112/117 docs, and 28/117 segments need one in their default `Template()`. I'd told you the facet was fictional and dropped it. It's restored — and now derived exactly rather than curated, by calling `Template()` on each registered writer in a Go test.

2. **Hydration.** Docusaurus SSRs `<StaticRouter location={pathname}>` — pathname only, no query. Initialising filter state from `useLocation().search` means `/segments?group=cli` renders 39 cards on the client against 117 in the server HTML, and React 19 throws the whole server tree away. My "don't touch `window`" instruction wouldn't have helped, because `useLocation()` is the leak. Fixed with `useIsBrowser()`.

Also fixed: card fill was `--ifm-background-surface-color`, which is `#fff` in light mode — border with no fill; the auth tag colour was 3.44:1, below AA; the description extractor would have silently shipped a WSL caution notice as `battery`'s description; and the termcard background didn't match `hero.png`'s actual baked-in `#173448`.

**One structural change I made on the review's evidence, worth your eye:** the drift guard moved from the website build into a Go test. `code.yml` carries `paths-ignore: ['website/**']` and `docs.yml` only runs on push to `main`, so a website-side guard would never have fired on a Go PR — it'd have broken a later deploy instead. The Go test also gives exact Nerd Font detection with no Go-source regex parsing, and drops the cross-boundary file read that `docusaurus build` couldn't reliably do inside the Azure SWA action.

That adds `src/config/segment_catalog_test.go` and a committed `website/plugins/segments/registry.json` to what was meant to be a website-only phase. Say the word if you'd rather keep Go untouched and accept a weaker guard.

`/segments` lands standalone; the docs index and the navbar retarget land after it, since `onBrokenLinks: 'throw'` fails any build that links a route that doesn't exist yet.

test(config): assert the segment registry matches the docs

Adding a segment means touching the registry, the docs and the sidebar by
hand, and nothing checked that those stayed in agreement. A segment could be
registered with no documentation, or documented after being removed, and the
first sign would be a reader hitting a page that no longer describes anything.

Derive the catalog from the live registry instead: call Template() on every
registered writer to find which segments need a Nerd Font glyph, then assert
a bidirectional match against the doc files. The result is written to
website/plugins/segments/registry.json, which the website consumes.

The test lives here rather than in the website build because the website is
not built on pull requests: code.yml ignores website/**, and docs.yml only
runs on push to main. A guard in the Docusaurus build would have caught drift
one deploy too late, and blamed whoever pushed next.

On mismatch the test rewrites the JSON as well as failing, so the fix is to
rerun it and stage the result rather than hand-edit a generated file.

Repo: D:\oh-my-posh, Go module root is `src/`. I am planning to extract a "run stream" (a sequence of styled text runs: text + foreground + background + attributes) as an intermediate representation inside the `terminal` package, so that ANSI becomes one encoder among several (SVG being the next). I need the current architecture mapped precisely before touching anything.

Investigate `src/terminal/` exhaustively and report with file:line references:

1. **Package-level state.** List EVERY package-level variable in `src/terminal/`. For each: name, type, what writes it, what reads it. I know there is at least `builder`, `length`, `cellIndex`, `foregroundColor`, `currentColor`, `bgGradientCells`. Give me the complete list, and say which are reset per-render and where the reset happens.

2. **The public API.** What functions does `terminal` export? Which are called from outside the package? Give the exact call sites (search `src/prompt/`, `src/cli/`, `src/segments/`). I want the full external surface.

3. **The write path.** Trace `Write(background, foreground, text)` (or whatever the main entry is) end to end. Where does styled text get turned into ANSI escape bytes? Is there a single choke point, or is escape-sequence emission scattered? Quote the key functions.

4. **What information is lost.** At the point ANSI bytes are emitted, what is known that the ANSI output does not preserve? Specifically: does the writer know segment boundaries, block boundaries, hyperlinks, cell widths, gradient stops? Where would a run stream need to be captured to keep those?

5. **Hyperlinks, and any other non-color escape.** How are OSC 8 hyperlinks handled? Any other non-SGR escapes emitted (cursor movement, OSC 7, title setting, bracketed paste)? These matter because an SVG encoder must handle or deliberately drop each one.

6. **Width/measurement.** Where is `go-runewidth` used, and what depends on `length`/`cellIndex`? Is the width calculation coupled to the ANSI emission, or separable?

7. **Existing tests and benchmarks.** List test files in `src/terminal/` and any `Benchmark*` functions anywhere in `src/` that exercise the prompt render path. I need to know what safety net already exists.

Report findings only, no recommendations. Be exhaustive on 1, 3 and 4 — those decide whether this refactor is safe.

1. **`src/cli/image/`** — full inventory. For `image.go` specifically: how does it obtain its input? Does it re-parse an ANSI string? Show the parsing code — what escape sequences does it understand, and which does it ignore or mishandle? Quote the parser loop.

2. **Font handling.** How does it get fonts today? I believe it downloads Hack.zip from GitHub at runtime around image.go:236. Confirm, and report: what font files, what fallback when the download fails, how are Nerd Font glyphs measured and drawn, and what is the "additional width for Nerd Font glyphs" fudge around image.go:498 compensating for?

3. **Layout model.** Does it lay out on a fixed character grid (one advance width per cell) or measure each glyph? Find `spaceAdvance` and explain how a wide/ambiguous-width character is handled.

4. **Dependencies.** Which third-party Go modules does `src/cli/image/` pull in that nothing else in the repo uses? Check `src/go.mod` and grep the rest of `src/` to confirm they are exclusive to the imager. I want an exact list plus line counts, because the deletion size decides a design question.

6. **`src/cli/data.go`** — how does `applyDataFile` work, and what exactly does it pin? I want to know how hermetic the engine becomes: does it disable live segment execution entirely, or only override values?

7. **The website pipeline.** `website/export_themes.mjs` — what does it shell out to, with which flags, and what does it produce? How many PNGs and how much disk do they occupy under `website/static/img/themes`?

8. **Any existing SVG or alternative output.** Grep for "svg" anywhere in `src/`. Is there prior art?

Report findings only, no recommendations. Be precise on 1, 2 and 4.

Your config is close to a worst case for this work, which makes it a good acceptance test:

- **`rprompt`** — a right-aligned block, which needs terminal width to position. SVG has no terminal, so width becomes an explicit parameter rather than an ambient fact.
- **`shell_integration` + `iterm_features`** — these emit OSC 133/1337 sequences that are *not visual*. An SVG encoder must drop them, and today they're interleaved into the same byte stream as the colors.
- 3 styles (diamond, plain, powerline), 5 `background_templates`, 8 leading diamonds, a palette, `min_width`.

That already argues where the seam goes: below template resolution, above escape emission, so non-visual escapes never enter the run stream at all.

content.text:
Diagnosis confirmed, and it's a real bug with direct bearing on this phase.

`--data` replay bypasses `Enabled()` ([segment.go:203-205](src/config/segment.go:203)), but `Time.Format` is *computed inside* `Enabled()` ([time.go:27-28](src/segments/time.go:27)). So a pinned `time` segment renders empty and its whole block disappears. Supplying `Format` explicitly brings it back — 419 bytes, renders `10:41:00`.

That matters because the render endpoint plan rests on `--data` being hermetic. Checking whether the existing exporter round-trips correctly.

content.text:
That comparison is confounded — the recorded data came from *my* machine (real git state, real path), so "more text" doesn't prove the bug. Discarding it as evidence.

Here's where the analysis lands.

## Phase 2 analysis

### The safety net works — but not the way I described it

Naive golden files fail: **46 of 122 themes are non-deterministic**. Cause is `website/segment_data.json`, which pins 24 of 117 segments; everything else runs live against the clock and filesystem.

Recording per-theme with `config export data` first gives **122/122 deterministic**, verified twice. That's the harness.

### A real bug in `--data`, and this phase depends on it

`restoreData` returns at [segment.go:203](src/config/segment.go:203), *before* `segment.writer.Enabled()` at `:243`. But `Time.Format` is computed inside `Enabled()` ([time.go:27](src/segments/time.go:27)). So pinning `time` with only `CurrentDate` makes the segment render empty — and its entire rprompt block silently vanishes, 419 bytes → 328. Adding `Format` restores it.

**14 of the 24 segments pinned in `website/segment_data.json` assign derived state inside `Enabled()`** (aws 9, strava 7, git 6, battery 5, gcp 4…). A hand-written data file must reproduce all of it exactly, with no validation and silent failure.

The recorder gets this right because it captures post-`Enabled()` state. So: hand-written data files are unsound, and `website/segment_data.json` is hand-written. I have **not** demonstrated a currently-visible defect on the site — my attempt to measure that was confounded by environment, and I'm not going to claim it.

### The seam is not where I told you it was

I said "extract a run stream between resolver and encoder in `terminal/`". That doesn't work as stated:

- **Semantic colour is destroyed at [writer.go:377](src/terminal/writer.go:377)**, before anything is written. `asAnsiColors` collapses `#FF5733`, `p:accent`, `parentBackground` and gradients into an SGR payload string like `"48;2;255;87;51"`. Gradient stops and the Apple Terminal 256-colour downgrade are gone irreversibly.
- **Segment identity doesn't exist in `terminal` at all.** `Write` is called once per *fragment* — leading diamond, text, separator, trailing diamond are four separate calls from `prompt/engine.go`. Block boundaries are implied only by `String()`.

So `data-segment`/`data-block` attributes can't come from a `terminal`-only run stream. Capture has to straddle `prompt/engine.go` for structure, or colour resolution has to move later.

### The refactor has a better justification than SVG

There are **three independent copies of the same tokenizer** — `writeBody:484`, `writeBodyGradient:543`, `countVisibleCells:894` — which [writer.go:886-892](src/terminal/writer.go:886) documents must stay in lockstep by hand. That's worth fixing on its own merits.

Two latent bugs found in passing: `isHyperlink` is never reset anywhere, so one unbalanced `<LINK>` corrupts every subsequent `Write` for the process lifetime; and OSC 8 emission has no `Plain` guard, so `--plain` still emits hyperlink escapes.

### The deletion is ~20x what I estimated

I said ≈1,500 lines and 3 dependencies. Actual: 1,877 first-party + ~27,700 third-party = **~29,600 lines**, 4 modules (`gg`, `stackblur`, `x/image`, `freetype`), verified exclusive by `go list -deps` set difference. The no-build-tag conclusion holds much more strongly than I argued.

### The current imager is worse than "re-parses ANSI"

Map iteration over prefix-overlapping regexes means **the same input can parse differently between runs**. 256-colour `\x1b[38;5;Nm` isn't handled at all — those bytes get drawn as visible glyphs. Bold and italic can't coexist. Strikethrough is parsed and discarded. Hyperlink URLs are dropped. And a font-download failure **exits 0 with no image**, so a CI run without network silently publishes nothing.

### Benchmark gate: allocations, not time

ns/op swings 8x run-to-run on this box (1492–11816 for one benchmark); B/op and allocs/op are exactly stable. Baseline captured: `BenchmarkEnginePrimary` 9,150 B / 95 allocs, `BenchmarkWriteAnchors` 602 B / 14 allocs.

## What I'd change about the plan

Split what was one phase into three, because the first part is independently valuable and shippable:

| | |
|---|---|
| **2.0** | Golden harness over 122 themes from recorded data; fix or hard-fail the `Enabled()`-bypass in `restoreData`; regenerate `segment_data.json` via the recorder |
| **2.1** | Collapse the three tokenizers into one; de-globalize enough to make capture possible. This is the actual risk, and it's justified without SVG |
| **2.2** | Run stream + SVG encoder + `--format svg` |

input.content:
# Phase 2.0 — Deterministic replay and the golden harness

The safety net for the renderer work, plus the correctness bug found while building it.
No run stream, no SVG, no changes to `terminal/`.

## Verified facts this plan rests on

| Fact | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `restoreData` returns before `writer.Enabled()` is ever called | `src/config/segment.go:203-205` vs `:243` |
| `Time.Format` is computed inside `Enabled()`, so replay renders it empty | `src/segments/time.go:27-28` |
| Pinning `time` with only `CurrentDate` silently drops the whole rprompt block | measured: 419 → 328 bytes on `themes/agnosterplus.omp.json` |
| Adding `Format` to the pinned data restores it exactly | measured: 419 bytes, renders `10:41:00` |
| 53 of 102 `Enabled()` implementations assign template-visible state | scan of receiver-field assignments |
| At least 24 of those perform direct I/O (`RunCommand`, `HasFiles`, `HTTPRequest`, …) | scan; more do so transitively |
| `website/segment_data.json` pins 24 of 117 segments; the rest run live | `src/config/segment.go:487-507` (`DataKey`) |
| With that hand-written file, 46 of 122 themes render non-deterministically | two full sweeps, diffed |
| With per-theme `config export data` recordings, 122 of 122 are deterministic | two full sweeps, diffed |
| The recorder captures post-`Enabled()` state, including `Format` | `tokyo.json` and friends contain every derived field |
| Recorded fixtures are ~580 KB; goldens ~237 KB | `du` over 122 files each |
| **Every recorded fixture contains the recording machine's real username** | 122/122 contain `jande` |
| **No theme PNG is tracked in git** — they are generated in CI only | `git ls-files 'website/static/img/themes/*'` returns 0 |
| ns/op varies ~8x run to run on this hardware; B/op and allocs/op are exactly stable | `-count=3` baseline |

Baseline to hold: `BenchmarkEnginePrimary` 9,150 B / 95 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteAnchors` 602 B / 14 allocs;
`BenchmarkWritePlainASCII` 280 B / 6 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteSolid` 465 B / 16 allocs;
`BenchmarkWriteGradient` 1,762 B / 17 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteGradientChained` 789 B / 27 allocs.

## Decisions already taken

- Ship Phase 2.0 on its own, before the tokenizer refactor.
- **Hermetic by default, derive by opt-in.** Replay never calls `Enabled()` unless explicitly
  asked. This is what keeps the golden harness deterministic and keeps a future render endpoint
  free of live segment execution — the `http`, `owm`, `nba`, `ipify`, `todoist` and `wakatime`
  segments all take a URL or key from config, so any path that runs them server-side is an SSRF
  proxy.

## Deliberately out of scope

The run stream, the SVG encoder, the tokenizer collapse, deleting `cli/image/`, and the
missing `Plain` guard on OSC 8 hyperlink emission (it changes ANSI output, so it must land
after the harness exists, not with it).

---

## Task A — the replay contract

**Owns:** `src/config/data.go`, `src/config/segment.go`, `src/cli/data.go`,
`src/cli/config_export_data.go`, and their tests.

Three changes, in this order.

### A1. Mark recorded files

The recorder writes a provenance marker into the file it produces. A top-level field on the
`Data` struct — a schema version is better than a bare boolean because it gives the next change
somewhere to go:

```json
{ "version": 1, "env": { … }, "segments": { … } }
```

Absent field means "hand-written", which is the current state of every existing file.

### A2. Fail loudly on unmarked data

On load, a file without the marker is a hard error naming the two ways forward:

> `<path>` was not produced by `oh-my-posh config export data`. Hand-written data files skip
> the segment's `Enabled()` step, so any field it derives will be missing and the segment can
> render empty. Record the file with `oh-my-posh config export data --config <config>
> --output <path>`, or pass `--data-derive` to compute derived state at render time.

The error must say *why*, not just *what*. The failure this replaces is silent and looks like
a theme bug.

### A3. `--data-derive`

An opt-in flag on the commands that accept `--data` (`print`, `config export image`). When set,
`restoreData` calls `segment.writer.Enabled()` first and unmarshals the pinned data **over** the
result, so derived fields are computed and pinned fields still win.

Order matters and is the whole point: `Enabled()` then overlay. The reverse recomputes over the
pinned values and discards them.

Document on the flag, in one line, that this re-runs live segment probes and is therefore
neither hermetic nor deterministic — it exists so a hand-written file stays usable locally.

**Verification:** `themes/agnosterplus.omp.json` with a data file containing only
`{"time":{"CurrentDate":"2026-01-01T09:41:00Z"}}` renders the time segment under
`--data-derive` and errors without it. Confirm the recorded-fixture path never calls `Enabled()`
— assert it, do not assume it, because that assertion is what the SSRF argument rests on.

---

## Task B — sanitized fixtures and the golden harness

**Owns:** a fixture-generation command or script, `src/prompt/golden_test.go` (or wherever
Task B judges correct after reading the existing test layout), and the committed fixtures.

### B1. Sanitize on record

**Recorded data cannot be committed as-is.** All 122 fixtures I generated contain my real
username, and the `env` block carries `UserName`, `HostName`, `PWD`, `AbsolutePWD`, `PSWD` and
`Folder`. Segment data embeds real paths too — `tokyo.json` contains a rendered template string
with the username in it, so scrubbing the `env` block alone is not enough.

Sanitization must therefore be a string-level pass over the whole serialized file, replacing the
recording machine's identity with fixed synthetic values, then the `env` block overwritten with:

```
UserName  alice
HostName  contoso-devbox
PWD       ~/dev/oh-my-posh
```

matching the values `website/segment_data.json` already uses, so the fixtures and the website
tell the same story.

**A test must assert no fixture contains the current user's name, hostname, or home path.**
Without it this regresses the first time someone regenerates on their own machine, and it
regresses silently into a public repo.

### B2. The harness

For each of the 122 bundled themes: render `print primary` with the sanitized fixture and
compare byte-for-byte against a committed golden.

- Fixtures ~580 KB, goldens ~237 KB. Acceptable; do not compress, a readable diff is the point.
- Failure output must show the first differing byte offset and a decoded escape context window.
  A diff of two ANSI blobs is unreadable otherwise, and this harness exists to be read during
  a refactor.
- Regeneration must be one documented command, and the test must name it on failure.
- The golden is the *current* output. This phase changes no rendering. If generating goldens
  produces a diff against what the current binary emits, stop and report — that is a bug found,
  not a golden to bless.

Wire into the workflow that runs on Go pull requests. Note `.github/workflows/code.yml` carries
`paths-ignore: ['website/**']`, which is fine here since everything lands under `src/`.

---

## Task C — make the website's data file valid

**Owns:** `website/segment_data.json`, `website/export_themes.mjs`, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`
if needed.

`website/segment_data.json` is hand-written and deliberately synthetic — it exists to make theme
screenshots look like a plausible machine, not to reflect any real one. Under A2 it now fails to
load.

Determine which of the two applies and implement it, reporting which and why:

Verified. My plan was built on a false premise, and I need to say so plainly.

## The review killed my plan. Three of the findings are mine to own.

**`--data` replay is not hermetic, and my 122/122 determinism was an artifact.**

The recorder skips disabled segments — [`if !segment.Enabled { continue }`](src/cli/config_export_data.go:129). So a fixture only covers what happened to be live on the recording machine, and everything else falls through to live execution:

| theme | configured | recorded | replay |
|---|---|---|---|
| tokyo | 16 | 9 | 0.08s |
| atomic | 24 | 9 | 0.08s |
| **chips** | 15 | 5 | **1.22s** |

That 1.22s is `wakatime` making a real HTTP call on the supposedly hermetic path. My determinism sweep passed only because the fixture's `PWD` doesn't exist, so every filesystem probe failed identically — change that path and it collapses. The SSRF constraint I carried into this phase from the start rests on the same false premise.

**Two more of mine:** there are **124** themes, not 122 — I globbed `*.omp.json` and missed two YAML themes, which go through a different unmarshal path and would have had zero coverage. And my citation of `DataKey` pointed at `restoreData`'s line range.

## Three that would have failed in CI

- **Timezone.** 65 themes carry a `time` segment, and `date` renders in the *renderer's* local zone. I demonstrated this myself without noticing: I pinned `09:41:00Z` and it rendered `10:41:00`. CI runners are UTC; my goldens would fail on every one.
- **`TERM_PROGRAM`.** [`color.TrueColor = Program != AppleTerminal`](src/terminal/writer.go:192) gates truecolor vs 256-colour emission. Same theme, same fixture, different bytes under macOS Terminal.app — and `code.yml` runs tests on all three OSes.
- **`prompt.New` reads the session cache** ([gob.go:44](src/config/gob.go:44)), so a harness looping over themes gets whatever config is cached, or the developer's own if `POSH_SESSION_ID` is set — which it is inside any real omp shell.

## And one design error

My A2 — hard-fail on unmarked data files — is a **breaking change to a feature shipped in v29.35.3**. [`data.mdx:54`](website/docs/configuration/data.mdx:54) explicitly teaches the opposite: *"A key left out falls back to the real environment, so specify only the properties your config depends on."* My plan had no docs task and would have broken every user following that page.

Also: Task C option 1 is circular, as the review put it — reproducing `segment_data.json` by recording would need a machine with AWS, Azure, GCP, kubectl, Terraform, Strava and Spotify all simultaneously authenticated. That's *why* it's hand-written.

## What this means for the phase

The centrepiece isn't the harness any more — it's the recorder. Record every segment with an explicit enabled flag, and make `restoreData` suppress recorded-but-disabled segments so they never probe. Only then is replay hermetic, only then is the harness meaningful, and only then does the render endpoint have a safety story.

That's a bigger, more invasive change than "build a safety net," and it lands in the same `Execute` path the tokenizer refactor will touch.

input.content:
# Phase 2.0 — Hermetic replay and the golden harness

The safety net for the renderer work, plus the correctness bug found while building it.
No run stream, no SVG, no tokenizer changes.

**Revision 2.** The first draft rested on a false premise: that `--data` replay is hermetic.
It is not. Every change from that draft is marked **[R]**.

## The premise that was wrong

`config export data` skips segments that were not enabled on the recording machine —
`src/cli/config_export_data.go:129-131`:

```go
for _, segment := range block.Segments {
    if !segment.Enabled {
        continue
    }
```

So a fixture covers only what happened to be live when it was recorded, and every other segment
falls through `restoreData` (`src/config/segment.go:488-491`, returns `false`) into the live
`segment.writer.Enabled()` at `:243`.

| theme | segments configured | recorded | replay |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tokyo | 16 | 9 | 0.08s |
| atomic | 24 | 9 | 0.08s |
| jandedobbeleer | 17 | 8 | 0.07s |
| **chips** | 15 | 5 | **1.22s** |

The 1.22s is `wakatime` making a live HTTP request during what was supposed to be a replay.

The earlier "122/122 deterministic" measurement was an artifact: the fixture's `PWD` does not
exist, so every filesystem probe failed identically on both sweeps. It proves nothing.

## Verified facts

| Fact | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `restoreData` returns before `writer.Enabled()` | `src/config/segment.go:203-205` vs `:243` |
| `Time.Format` is computed inside `Enabled()`, so replay renders it empty | `src/segments/time.go:27-28` |
| Pinning `time` with only `CurrentDate` drops the whole rprompt block, silently | measured 419 → 328 bytes on `agnosterplus` |
| Adding `Format` restores it | measured 419 bytes, renders `10:41:00` |
| 53 of 102 `Enabled()` implementations assign template-visible state; ≥24 do I/O | scan |
| **The recorder skips disabled segments** | `src/cli/config_export_data.go:129-131` |
| **124 themes, not 122** — 122 `.omp.json` plus 2 `.omp.yaml` | `ls themes/*.omp.*` |
| **65 themes carry a `time` segment** | `grep -l '"type": *"time"'` |
| **`date` renders in the renderer's local zone** | pinned `09:41:00Z` rendered `10:41:00` here |
| **`color.TrueColor = Program != AppleTerminal`** gates truecolor vs 256-colour | `src/terminal/writer.go:192`, read at `src/color/colors.go:312` |
| **`prompt.New` returns the session-cached config, ignoring the path** | `src/config/gob.go:44-49`, called from `src/prompt/engine.go:804-806` |
| **`--data` shipped in v29.35.3 and `data.mdx` documents partial hand-written files** | `website/docs/configuration/data.mdx:54-55` |
| **No bundled theme uses `<LINK>`** | `grep -l '<LINK>' themes/*.omp.*` returns 0 |
| `isHyperlink` is reset in neither `Write`'s prologue nor `String()`'s cleanup | `writer.go:78`, `:385-392`, `:605-619` |
| `DataKey` is the segment `Alias` or `Type` | `src/config/segment.go:412-418` |
| No theme PNG is tracked in git | `git ls-files 'website/static/img/themes/*'` → 0 |
| ns/op swings ~8x on this hardware; B/op and allocs/op are exactly stable | `-count=3` |
| `LoadData` reads only `env` and `segments`, tolerating unknown top-level keys | `src/config/data.go:43-90` |

Baseline to hold: `BenchmarkEnginePrimary` 9,150 B / 95 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteAnchors` 602 B /
14 allocs; `BenchmarkWritePlainASCII` 280 B / 6 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteSolid` 465 B / 16 allocs;
`BenchmarkWriteGradient` 1,762 B / 17 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteGradientChained` 789 B / 27 allocs.

## Decisions taken

- Ship Phase 2.0 alone, before the tokenizer refactor.
- **[R] Fix the recorder properly.** Record every configured segment with an explicit enabled
  flag; `restoreData` suppresses recorded-but-disabled segments without probing. Hermeticity has
  to be real before the harness or any render endpoint can lean on it.
- **[R] No breaking change.** Hand-written partial files keep working, with a warning and
  correctly derived state. `data.mdx:54` documents them and `--data` shipped in v29.35.3.

## Out of scope

The run stream, the SVG encoder, the tokenizer collapse, deleting `cli/image/`, the missing
`Plain` guard on OSC 8 emission, recording tooltip segments (`buildDataDocument` iterates
`cfg.Blocks` only, `config_export_data.go:127`), and changing the `DataKey` scheme.

**[R] Known limitation to document, not fix:** themes with two segments of the same type and no
`alias` collide on `DataKey` — the recorder already warns `multiple segments share the data key
"text"; the last one wins`. Goldens will encode that lossy behaviour. That is acceptable: the
harness is a change-detector, and the behaviour it locks in is the current one.

---

## Task A — make replay hermetic

**Owns:** `src/cli/config_export_data.go`, `src/config/data.go`, `src/config/segment.go`,
`src/cli/data.go`, `website/docs/configuration/data.mdx`, and their tests.

### A1. Record everything

Drop the `!segment.Enabled` skip. Record every configured segment, carrying its enabled state:

```json
{ "version": 1, "env": { … }, "segments": { "git": { "enabled": true, "data": { … } } } }
```

Shape is Task A's call, but the enabled flag must be per segment and must survive round-trip.
Keep backward compatibility with the current flat shape, since `website/segment_data.json` and
every user file use it.

`version` is safe to add: `LoadData` decodes the root into `map[string]json.RawMessage` and
reads only `env` and `segments`, so unknown top-level keys are already tolerated on the JSON,
YAML and TOML paths.

### A2. Suppress recorded-but-disabled segments

In `restoreData`:

- present and enabled → current behaviour: unmarshal the pinned data, `Enabled = true`, return
  `true`. No probe.
- **[R]** present and disabled → `Enabled = false`, `restored = true`, return `true`. **No
  probe.** This is the case that makes replay hermetic.
- absent → return `false` and fall through, as today.

**[R]** Do not move the recorded path's short-circuit. It sits at `:203`, before
`shouldHideForWidth` (`:212`) and the `runjobs` Job setup (`:227-241`). That bypass exists
today; changing it would change rendered output, and this phase's entire purpose is to
establish a baseline before output changes. File the width-hiding gap separately.

### A3. Warn and derive for unmarked files

A file without `version` is hand-written. Keep it working:

- Warn once per run, naming the file, saying it is neither hermetic nor deterministic, and
  giving the recorder command.
- For segments present in it, compute derived state so they stop silently vanishing.
- For segments absent from it, fall back to the live environment — the documented contract at
  `data.mdx:54-55`.

**[R] Where the derive happens matters.** Do **not** short-circuit at `:203` for this path.
Let `Execute` run normally so `Enabled()` fires at `:243` and then overlay the pinned data on
top. Short-circuiting at `:203` would skip `shouldHideForWidth` (`:212`), the `runjobs` Job
creation and its `defer` (`:227-241`) — so a pinned segment with a `timeout` would spawn live
child processes with no Job object, and `KillGoroutineChildren` could not terminate them on
Windows — and `segment.evaluated = true` at `:244`, leaving `renderFallback` (`:297`) dead.

Order is `Enabled()` then overlay, never the reverse. `json.Unmarshal` into the existing writer
preserves fields absent from the JSON, so pinned values win and derived values fill the gaps.

Add `--data-derive` to force this path for a recorded file too, for local debugging.

**[R] Note and document:** `restoreData` sets `Enabled = true` unconditionally, so a pinned
segment renders even where its live check would suppress it — `battery` on a machine without
one. That is today's behaviour and stays; say so in the docs rather than leaving it implicit.

### A4. Docs

Update `website/docs/configuration/data.mdx`: the recorder is the recommended path and the only
hermetic one; hand-written partial files still work and now derive correctly; the `version`
marker; the `alias` workaround for duplicate segment types.

**Verification:** `agnosterplus` with `{"time":{"CurrentDate":"2026-01-01T09:41:00Z"}}` renders
the time segment (it does not today). `chips` replayed from a re-recorded fixture makes **zero**
network calls and drops from 1.22s to the ~0.08s the other themes take. That timing is the
hermeticity proof — assert it, because the SSRF argument for any future render endpoint rests
on it.

---

## Task B — sanitized fixtures and the golden harness

**Owns:** the sanitizer, the harness test, the committed fixtures, and the `newEngine`
extraction below. Depends on Task A.

### B1. Sanitize structurally, not by string replace

**[R] A naive replace both corrupts and misses.** Case-insensitively replacing the username
rewrites `https://github.com/JanDeDobbeleer/oh-my-posh` in recorded git data into
`aliceDobbeleer`; case-sensitively, it misses `C:\Users\Jande` and `%USERNAME%` in caps.

And the identity is not confined to the `env` block. Recorded fixtures carry:

- `Segment.Text` — the fully rendered string, e.g. `" jande@surface-pro "`
- `git.User.Name` / `git.User.Email` — the real git author identity
- `aws.AccessKeyID`; `az` `TenantID`, `HomeTenantID`, subscription IDs, `User.Name` (an email)

- the hostname, which is often a device model

`alice` / `contoso-devbox` / `~/dev/oh-my-posh`, matching `website/segment_data.json` so the

recomputed on render anyway; (c) applies a per-field scrub list covering the above; (d)
normalises `sysinfo` and `battery` to fixed values.

denylist test for `AccessKeyID`, `User.Email` and `TenantID`. The backstop is not the mechanism
— it is what catches the next person regenerating on their own machine, before it reaches a
public repo.

`code.yml` runs `go test ./...` on ubuntu, macos and windows.

   verified no effect on Windows.

   explicitly, before `terminal.Init`. Otherwise macOS Terminal.app emits 256-colour and every
   golden fails.

runtime.Environment) *Engine`, call it from both `New` and the harness, and have the harness use
`config.Load(path)` directly.

---
name: omp-data-replay-not-hermetic
description: "--data replay is not hermetic: the recorder skips disabled segments, so unrecorded ones still probe live"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Discovered 2026-07-26 while building a golden-file harness for the renderer work.

`oh-my-posh config export data` skips segments that were not enabled on the recording
machine (`src/cli/config_export_data.go:129-131`, `if !segment.Enabled { continue }`).
A fixture therefore covers only what happened to be live at record time; everything else
falls through `restoreData` (`src/config/segment.go:488-491` returns false) into the live
`writer.Enabled()` at `:243`. Measured: `themes/chips.omp.json` records 5 of 15 segments and
"replays" in **1.22s** because `wakatime` makes a real HTTP call, versus ~0.08s for themes
whose segments were all captured.

Two consequences that cost a full replan:

1. **Any "golden files over the bundled themes" measurement is suspect.** An early sweep
   showed 122/122 deterministic; that was an artifact — the fixture's pinned `PWD` does not
   exist, so every filesystem probe failed identically on both runs.
2. **The SSRF argument for a server-side render endpoint does not hold on replay alone.**
   `http`, `owm`, `nba`, `ipify`, `todoist` and `wakatime` all take a URL or key from config.
   Until the recorder captures every segment *and* `restoreData` suppresses recorded-but-
   disabled ones without probing, a data file is not a safety boundary.

Related: `restoreData` returns before `Enabled()`, and 53 of 102 segments assign
template-visible state inside `Enabled()` (≥24 of those do I/O). So a hand-written partial
file silently renders those segments empty — pinning `time` with only `CurrentDate` drops
the whole rprompt block, because `Time.Format` is computed in `Enabled()`
(`src/segments/time.go:27-28`).

**Why:** three separate plans were built on "replay is hermetic" before it was measured.

**How to apply:** never treat a `--data` file as a hermetic or security boundary without
first checking the recorder covers every configured segment. Verify hermeticity by *timing*
a replay, not by diffing two runs — identical output can mean uniformly failing probes.
See [[omp-golden-harness-ambient-inputs]] for what else makes theme renders non-reproducible.

Found 2026-07-26 while scoping a golden-file harness over the bundled themes. Any test that
renders themes and compares bytes must neutralise all of these, or it fails on CI (which runs
ubuntu, macos and windows) while passing locally.

  `time` segment. Set `time.Local = time.UTC` in `TestMain`; setting `TZ` does not work on
  Windows.
- **`TERM_PROGRAM` / `WT_SESSION`.** `color.TrueColor = Program != AppleTerminal`
  (`src/terminal/writer.go:192`) gates truecolor versus 256-colour emission
  (`src/color/colors.go:312`). Same theme and fixture produce different bytes under
  macOS Terminal.app. Unset both, or set `terminal.Program` explicitly, before `terminal.Init`.
- **The session cache.** `segment.isToggled()` (`src/config/segment.go:424-437`) reads
  `TOGGLECACHE` and returns *before* `restoreData`, so anyone who has run `oh-my-posh toggle`
  gets different output. Point `cache.Path()` at a temp dir and do not call `cache.Close()`.
- **`prompt.New` ignores the config path.** It calls `config.Get`, which returns the
  session-cached config (`src/config/gob.go:44-49`) — inside a real omp shell that is the
  developer's own config, not the theme under test. But hand-rolling the Engine skips what
  `New` does after `config.Get` (`terminal.Plain`, `forceRender`, `Grow(512)`, `HasExtra`,
  `rectifyTerminalWidth` for xonsh/elvish/pwsh, `engine.go:836-860`). Extract the second half
  of `New` so both paths share it.

Also: there are **124** themes, not 122 — `themes/*.omp.yaml` adds two, and YAML goes through a
separate `Segment.UnmarshalYAML` path (`segment.go:133-155`). Enumerate by the same extension
set `website/export_themes.mjs:18` uses.

Benchmark gate on this hardware: **ns/op swings ~8x run to run** (1492–11816 for one
benchmark); `B/op` and `allocs/op` are exactly stable. Gate on allocations, never on time.

**Why:** each of these was found only by an adversarial review of a plan that looked finished,
and every one of them fails in CI rather than locally.

**How to apply:** read this before writing any test that renders a prompt and compares output.
See [[omp-data-replay-not-hermetic]] for why the fixtures themselves need work first.
